and Coeur d'Alene metro this this morning, especially northern
Spokane County and the West Plains, including I-90 and US-2.

extra caution while traveling as visibilities can change quickly.

space between you and other vehicles. The fog is expected to lift
by mid-morning.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 18 at 9:38AM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
At 930 am, widespread showers and embedded thunderstorms are ongoing
across the Florida Keys and surrounding near and offshore waters.
This activity is producing pockets of higher wind gusts of 25 to near
34 knots, occasional bouts of lightning, and reduced visibility from
moderate to heavy downpours. Activity remains nearly stationary, but
is slowly circulating around a small scale area of low pressure
currently centered in the Straits of Florida approximately 20
nautical miles south of Key West. A few cells may intensify and
higher gusts and waterspouts will be possible, requiring a Special
Marine Warning.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and gusty winds expected. Total snow accumulations
of 2 to 4 inches with locally higher totals up to around 6
inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Western Interior.

* WHEN...Tuesday night through Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Relatively dry conditions are expected to
continue through this evening ahead of a front moving in late
tonight into early Wednesday. Highest totals could range as
high as 6 inches for the higher terrain and areas near McGrath
during this period.
